Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “fresh signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Industry observers note that ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT.

It has been revealed that defensive rebuilding is next summer’s big project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the concerns in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k.

United were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD.

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR.

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

According to recent reports, “There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick said. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”.

According to recent reports, there was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

Recent findings suggest that he recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

Sources indicate that asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick remarked, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”.

In a recent development, the Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”.

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He showed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a significant week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

Recent findings suggest that “There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”.

Industry observers note that speaking with Sky Sports, he stated: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

According to recent reports, “To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

According to recent reports, “But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”.

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx.

Sources indicate that the hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

Sources indicate that “Scoring before half-time is always crucial if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”.

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

The Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

According to recent reports, if the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. Industry observers note that sto bene. Sono felice di essere tornato a Roma. La prima è stata positiva, la seconda poteva andare meglio, ma sono felice di essere tornato a Roma. Nel fine settimana ci aspetta una partita importante e non vediamo l'ora di giocarla.

In a recent development, penso che quest'anno abbiamo iniziato molto bene con Gattuso. Direi che queste sono le caratteristiche che mi descrivono meglio.

Se riuscirò a fare tutto questo, penso che sarà una stagione davvero molto positiva, non soltanto per me, ma anche per tutti i ragazzi. Get German Football News explores the five best….

Recent findings suggest that flourishing at RB Leipzig since returning to the club on loan in the summer, Christopher Nkunku has returned five goals and provided two assists since returning to the Saxony club. The Frenchman provided an assist against Borussia Mönchengladbach on his second debut before opening his account at the Red Bull Arena in Leipzig’s 5-0 victory over Hamburg. The 29-year-old then struck a hat-trick against Eintracht Frankfurt before adding a goal and assist to his 2026/27 tally against Augsburg prior to the international break. Often starting in a three-pronged attack alongside Romulo and Antonio Nusa/Tidiam Gomis, Nkunku is given the freedom to roam by Martin Demichelis, which makes his a nuisance for opposition defenders. Ranked in the 95th percentile for xGoals on target (4.14), Nkunku has proved clinical in front of goal, scoring five of his eight attempts on target.

The Spaniard has massive boots to fill following the departure of Alejandro Grimaldo, but the former Napoli man is settling into life at Bayer Leverkusen just fine. The 25-year-old has scored one goal and created a further four in his nine Bundesliga starts since swapping Italy for Germany. Equally adept at playing as the left-sided centre-back in a back three, or as the left-back or left-wing back in a back four/five, no defender ranks higher in the Bundesliga than Gutiérrez for assists and big chances created (eight) in Germany’s top flight this season.

Sources indicate that hennes Behrens at €3.5m is proving to be a steal for Augsburg, who are proving to be one of the Bundesliga’s best recruiters. Joining from Hoffenheim after spending last season on loan at Heidenheim, the 21-year-old is proving a useful weapon from left-back, where he’s registered three assists in nine Bundesliga outings this term. Possessing explosive pace and pinpoint crossing, Behrens is fast becoming one of the league’s most useful full-backs in the final third.

Re-joining Werder Bremen on loan after a failed spell abroad, Niclas Füllkrug is firing on all cylinders back at the Weserstadion. The 33-year-old sits at the top of the Bundesliga’s scoring charts this term having scored nine goals in as many appearances – seven of those have come from set-piece situations. Playing with a smile on his face once again, it’s great to see Füllkrug back to his best, which has also seen him return to the German national team. Carry on, and Bremen could well be competing for a place in Europe if the veteran goal-getter remains injury free and keeps up his output.

According to recent reports, joining newly promoted Elversberg from Bayern Munich having spent last season on loan at 2. Bundesliga side Hertha Berlin, Maurice Krattenmacher has scored four goals and provided one assist in nine Bundesliga games this season – of which he’s only started four. The 21-year-old came off the bench to score a brace against Gladbach to secure a dramatic 4-3 victory for Vincent Wagner’s side, before netting against Bayern the following matchday with a superb curling effort. The attacking-midfielder also registered an assist and scored in wins of Augsburg and Mainz as the Bundesliga newcomers enjoy a magnificent start to their Bundesliga tenure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in his first press conference back from his illness-related absence, Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany offered an interesting perspective on Jamal Musiala’s impending return to competitive football. The Belgian suggested that the German international could benefit from the changing expectations surrounding him. Speaking at Thursday’s pre-match press conference ahead of Bayern’s Bundesliga encounter with Köln, Kompany also addressed recent remarks from honorary president Uli Hoeneß concerning the 23-year-old’s long-term prospects.

Musiala is expected to return to Bayern’s matchday squad on Friday, provided he encounters no setbacks during Thursday’s final training session. The attacking midfielder has been sidelined since suffering a significant thigh injury while warming up for Germany’s UEFA Nations League encounter with the Netherlands in September.

In a recent development, the latest setback interrupted an encouraging return to competitive football. Musiala has accumulated approximately 200 minutes this season, scoring in both of his starts. He opened the scoring in Bayern’s 5-0 Champions League victory over Bodø/Glimt and the 7-0 Bundesliga triumph over Union Berlin.

Sources indicate that musiala’s recovery has attracted additional attention following recent remarks from Uli Hoeneß questioning whether the midfielder can regain his previous performance level. Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen also raised questions about how the club might respond if Musiala’s performances were permanently affected. Sporting director Max Eberl sought to reassure supporters on Thursday, emphasizing the club’s continued belief in Musiala’s ability to rediscover his best form.

Kompany, meanwhile, adopted a different approach to the discussion. Rather than disagreeing with Bayern’s hierarchy, the Belgian emphasized that his responsibility as head coach requires him to maintain confidence in his players regardless of the concerns expressed elsewhere within the organization.

The Bayern trainer also suggested that Musiala’s changed circumstances could provide valuable motivation. Having previously enjoyed the status of an almost untouchable young star, the midfielder now has an opportunity to demonstrate his abilities without carrying precisely the same expectations.

It has been revealed that kompany drew a parallel between Musiala’s comeback and his own return following an extended absence due to illness. The coach expressed hope that both experiences could provide renewed energy for Bayern during the remainder of the season. The 40-year-old also praised Musiala’s determination throughout his rehabilitation, emphasizing that the youngster must ultimately demonstrate his recovery through performances on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that “We don’t have differing opinions,” Kompany added when questioned about Hoeneß’ comments on Musiala. “What we have is different roles. My role is to believe in all the players. That’s my role. It would be a catastrophe if I came here and stated that, for example, five specific players didn’t matter.”.

According to recent reports, “The fact that we have different roles is one of the things that function well at Bayern,” Kompany continued. “I have 100 percent respect for the opinions of the [club] hierarchy. I don’t have a problem with that. One has to put it into perspective and we can also utilize this in a sporting sense.”.

“There’s nothing that can serve as a greater motivation for a player like Jamal,” Kompany concluded. “There’s something he can show without the same pressure as when he was a ‘golden child’. This is also a nice moment. Luckily, the head coach has had plenty of such moments in his career and I’m looking forward to it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has spoken publicly about his recent health scare at his first press conference since returning to work. Appearing at Thursday’s pre-match press conference ahead of Friday’s Bundesliga encounter with Cologne, the 40-year-old reflected on the circumstances surrounding his collapse, his recovery, and the extraordinary support he received during his absence.

Kompany collapsed while observing a Bayern reserve-team training session on October 23 and was subsequently hospitalized. As Get German Football News reported at the time, sporting director Max Eberl later confirmed that doctors had diagnosed an irritation of the meninges.

The Belgian also sustained a shoulder injury during the incident, subsequently requiring surgery. Kompany appeared at Thursday’s press conference wearing a sling on his left arm, but emphasized that extensive medical examinations had provided reassurance about his general health.

The Bayern trainer acknowledged that the experience had been frightening, particularly given the unexpected nature of his collapse. Looking back, Kompany suggested that he had continued working while ill rather than giving his body the rest it required. The 40-year-old nevertheless expressed considerable relief that his medical examinations had not revealed anything requiring more serious intervention.

Kompany also took the opportunity to thank Bayern’s medical personnel, club officials, and the many individuals who had contacted him during his absence.

According to recent reports, the coach’s collapse prompted an outpouring of sympathy throughout German football. As Get German Football News documented in the aftermath, several Bundesliga coaches publicly reflected on the demanding nature of their profession while offering Kompany their best wishes.

The Belgian was particularly struck by the extent of the support he received, remarking that more people had contacted him during his illness than after his previous sporting successes.

“Actually, I have to say that I’m very healthy,” Kompany explained. “I’ve undergone plenty of tests. We tried to find something, but fortunately nothing was so serious that further measures were necessary.”.

“I was simply ill,” Kompany continued. “Perhaps I didn’t listen to my body enough, and everything that happened afterwards was simply a consequence of that.”.

“I received so much support,” the Bayern coach added. “More people contacted me than when I won titles.”.

  • Industry observers note that danks assumed responsibility for Bayern’s first team after Kompany collapsed during a reserve-team training session on October 23.
  • The results included a 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Freiburg, a 6-1 DFB-Pokal triumph against Magdeburg, a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund, a 2-0 Champions League win away at Atlético Madrid, and a 2-1 victory over Mainz.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has revealed that he deliberately refrained from making any coaching decisions during his recent absence, insisting that assistant coach Aaron Danks and the remaining staff deserved complete responsibility for the team. Speaking at Thursday’s press conference ahead of his return to the touchline against Cologne, the 40-year-old offered an interesting insight into his management philosophy and reflected on watching his team succeed from a distance.

Industry observers note that danks assumed responsibility for Bayern’s first team after Kompany collapsed during a reserve-team training session on October 23. The Belgian required hospitalization and an extended period away from his coaching duties. Bayern nevertheless maintained their unbeaten run under Danks, recording four victories and one draw across five competitive fixtures.

The results included a 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Freiburg, a 6-1 DFB-Pokal triumph against Magdeburg, a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund, a 2-0 Champions League win away at Atlético Madrid, and a 2-1 victory over Mainz.

Kompany emphasized that he had deliberately avoided interfering with his assistants’ decision-making throughout the period. Although he maintained contact with the coaching staff and discussed matches afterward, the Belgian insisted that his involvement was limited to understanding their decisions rather than influencing them. The arrangement reflected his conviction that stepping away from responsibility required allowing those taking his place to exercise genuine authority.

Kompany also expressed particular satisfaction with Bayern’s Champions League victory over Atlético Madrid. Watching his players support one another and overcome the Spanish side without him on the touchline represented one of the most memorable experiences of his coaching career. The period away from daily responsibilities also afforded Kompany an unusual opportunity for reflection.

The Bayern trainer suggested that coaches rarely receive the chance to consider their work from a fresh perspective without leaving their clubs. Although his absence was involuntary, he nevertheless found time to consider how Bayern might improve further upon his return.

“I didn’t make a single decision. Zero,” Kompany emphasized when discussing his absence at Thursday’s press conference. “But there’s an notable reason why I wasn’t involved in that decision-making process. You must respect the work. You can’t be there every day, then suddenly not be there anymore, and still insist on having an opinion and making decisions. You simply can’t do that.”.

“Ultimately, the best place to be is on the bench with the team,” the Bayern coach continued. “But I also enjoyed seeing how the lads stuck together. That really was one of the highlights of my career. As a coach, you never get the chance to have a reboot, a fresh start in your career at the same club. Usually, you have to do that somewhere else. In my case, that’s a luxury I now have.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Niko Kovac had an unusual concern to contend with ahead of Borussia Dortmund’s return to Bundesliga action: the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

Asked at Thursday’s press conference whether the eagerly anticipated video game had become a major topic inside the BVB dressing room, Kovac joked that he hoped none of his players had been staying up deep into the night playing it.

The Dortmund head coach conceded that several members of his squad were likely already heavily involved with the game, quipping that he hoped they would not “confuse day and night” ahead of Saturday’s trip to Borussia Mönchengladbach.

The light-hearted exchange came at the end of a press conference otherwise dominated by Dortmund’s need to hit the ground running following the international break.

BVB travel to bottom-of-the-table Gladbach on Saturday at 15:30 CET with 21 points from their opening nine Bundesliga matches. Kovac’s side remain unbeaten in league play and sit second, level on points with leaders Bayern Munich. Dortmund have also conceded only seven goals, the best defensive record in the division.

Sources indicate that “We can’t afford to take any time to get going,” Kovac mentioned. “There are still eight games left this year. In these games, we want to cement our place at the top of the Bundesliga. The other teams are pushing from behind. We have to be ready right away.”.

Saturday’s match begins another demanding stretch for Dortmund. BVB face eight competitive fixtures in 29 days before the winter break, having only just completed a run of nine matches across 29 of days prior to the November international break.

The experience of the previous international break also provides an obvious warning.

Dortmund failed to win any of their first three matches after returning to club action in October, drawing 2-2 with Werder Bremen and 0-0 with Union Berlin in the Bundesliga either side of a 1-0 Champions League defeat to Bodø/Glimt.

Kovac nevertheless believes the circumstances are somewhat different this time. The Dortmund coach noted that the latest international window involved a more conventional two-match schedule rather than the unusually heavy international programme surrounding the previous break, leaving his players closer to their normal competitive rhythm.

Recent findings suggest that getting into matches more promptly has become an increasingly prominent theme for Dortmund. BVB’s last ten Bundesliga goals have all arrived after half-time, an unusual run that Kovac would preferably bring to an end in Gladbach.

“If you take an early lead, the game opens up much more quickly,” Kovac said.

Sources indicate that the trend has done little damage to Dortmund’s results so far, but it has repeatedly forced BVB to remain patient before finding breakthroughs. Five of their nine Bundesliga matches this season have reached half-time without Dortmund scoring.

Industry observers note that kovac will also have several late personnel decisions to make. Serhou Guirassy, Waldemar Anton, and Carney Chukwuemeka remained in Dortmund during the international break while dealing with muscular problems. Kovac said that their availability would be assessed ahead of the weekend and stressed that “nothing is ruled out.”.

Samuele Inacio has meanwhile returned from international duty carrying a minor complaint, leaving another question mark over Dortmund’s squad for Saturday.

The mood became considerably lighter when Kovac was questioned about the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

In a recent development, A reporter asked whether the Dortmund coach had encountered an unusual number of players requesting a “sick day” following the game’s release and whether GTA had become a major topic inside the dressing room. Kovac was also asked whether he owned a PlayStation 5 himself.

In a recent development, “I don’t have one,” Kovac responded. “I reached the age at which I’m out. I believe I heard or read some time ago that this game was coming out. I hope my lads haven’t been playing deep into the night. How does one do something like that these days? Per App or does one need hardware [a gaming console]?”.

The reporter clarified that the game could be downloaded on a console, adding that BVB striker Fabio Silva had commented on downloading it in the three days since its release.

Recent findings suggest that “Okay, then I’ll act on the assumption that they [the players] are playing it,” Kovac continued. “I hope they don’t play it so excessively that they can’t tell day from night anymore. That could be problematic. But today is a wonderful day not just because of the fact that this game is being released, but because we also have two in-house birthdays with Costa [Konstantinos Karetsas] and Joey [Veerman].

According to recent reports, “That’s much more important than this game,” Kovac concluded. “But I have heard that a few [of the players] are intensively involved [with the video game].”.

Ligue 1 outfit AS Monaco have reached an agreement with German youth international Paris Brunner (20) regarding a contract extension beyond 2028, according to RMC Sport, as reported via our colleagues at Get French Football News.

The young attacker is expected to sign a contract through to 2030 after scoring eight goals and providing one assists in 13 matches for Monaco in 2026/27 after joining the Principality club from Borussia Dortmund in the summer in search of senior football, having not made an appearance for BVB’s first team.

Brunner’s performances also coincided with a run in Antonio Di Salvo’s Germany U21 squad during the recent international break where he featured in defeats against Belgium and Croatia. He was, though, one of the winners in Germany’s youth team, which also saw the youngster earn praise from Di Salvo. “Moving Paris [to the left] was something that we wanted as we wanted to have a player like that on the left [wing]. Brajan Gruda scored two goals and provided two assists in his first two appearances for the German national team against Serbia and the Netherlands over the recent international break and with four assists in seven Bundesliga games for RB Leipzig in 2026/27, the 22-year-old’s stock continues to rise.

On loan from Premier League side Brighton and Hove Albion, Gruda’s move to Leipzig will become permanent in the newly introduced year if he plays every match between now and Hoffenheim on 16 January. The fee: €25m. The newly capped German international will then pen a contract until July 2031, without a release clause.

It has been revealed that that ultimately means that Leipzig can command any fee they wish for their rising star. With interest from Liverpool and Bayern Munich, and with no intention of selling, BILD estimate Leipzig’s valuation of Gruda to be around €100m.

With impressive numbers across his first two Germany appearances, Gruda was naturally one of seven winners in Jürgen Klopp’s November squad.

Ethan Nwaneri (19) registered two assists in England U21s recent 3-2 victory over France, but the Borussia Dortmund man has struggled for playing time in the Bundesliga recently.

Recent findings suggest that speaking at Thursday’s press conference, BVB head coach Niko Kovač weighed in on the player’s situation. “We have very good players in those positions up front, he explained. Nwaneri initially replaced Giannis Konstantelias, who suffered an ACL injury on his Bundesliga debut against Hamburg, while Fabio Silva is shining alongside Serhou Guirassy, while Konstantinos Karetsas has recently returned from a back injury.

“The competition is tough,” added Kovač, who did praise Nwaneri’s performances for England. “As far as Ethan is concerned, we’re delighted,” he said. ” It was a friendly match and he did really well.”.

With an assist to his name on his Bundesliga but against Hoffenheim on Matchday 2, Nwaneri has featured in eight of nine possible league games, playing 336 minutes for Die Schwarzgelben in Germany’s top flight.

On Saturday, Dortmund face Borussia Mönchengladbach at Borussia-Park as they look to maintain their unbeaten start to their Bundesliga campaign.

Injuries are mounting up at Bayern Munich after Harry Kane and Michael Olise were both forced off with injuries against Cologne in Friday night’s Bundesliga clash.

Kane was replaced by Tom Bischof in the 20th minute with what looked to be an ankle injury after Mikey Moore had given Cologne a 1-0 lead at the Allianz Arena.

It has been revealed that nathaniel Brown then leveled proceedings for Germany’s record champions, minutes before Olise received treatment following a collision with Tom Krauß in the 41st minute.
